english.title: Breach of stalking protection order / interim stalking protection order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse, breached

(A)_[a stalking protection order]_
(B)_[an interim stalking protection order]_

made by **(..SPECIFY COURT..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE..), in that **(..SPECIFY BREACH..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 8(1) and (2) of the Stalking Protection Act 2019.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
a person
without reasonable excuse
conducted an act they were prohibited from doing by
a stalking protection order OR
an interim stalking protection order
breaching section 8(1) of the Stalking Protection Act 2019

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Persons under 18 may also be charged with this offence.
(ii) In proceedings for an offence under this section, a copy of the original stalking protection order / interim stalking protection order (certified by the designated officer for the court which made it) is admissible as evidence of it having been made and of its contents. This is to the same extent that oral evidence would be admissible in such proceedings.
(iii) If a person is convicted of an offence under this section, it is not open to the court by or before which the person is convicted to make a conditional discharge.

other.penalty:
Either way -Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force, the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment
